clue.text: Game birds initially put by kid into coop

indicators.note: the kid and bird letters are put into the coop word, so it surrounds them

parts.note: a coop is a cage for poultry

indicators.note: the first letter of birds is set beside the kid word, after it

parts.note: to kid is to tease, or rib

indicators.note: initially picks just the opening letter of birds

explanation.surface: A child shuts some birds into a hen coop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes only the B of birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Cribbage is a card game scored with pegs on a board.

clue.text: Lackey evidently revealing thighs?

parts.note: a miniskirt, a mini, is the garment that shows off the thighs
evidently, worn in plain view, is on, as a skirt you have on

explanation.surface: A servant seems to be showing a lot of leg.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a playful description: a short skirt is what shows the thighs, and 'evidently' gives the sense of being worn in view.
explanation.definitionFit: A minion is a servile follower, a synonym for lackey.

clue.text: French fighting, something common or vulgar?

parts.note: fighting is action, as in soldiers seeing action

explanation.surface: French combat that is crude or coarse in nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'common' and 'vulgar' look like insults, but common and vulgar fractions are school arithmetic terms.
explanation.definitionFit: A vulgar or common fraction is one written as numerator over denominator, so either kind is an example.

clue.text: Assess company lacking leadership that's about to struggle

indicators.note: about means the trimmed company word goes round the struggle word
lacking its leader means the word for company loses its first letter

parts.note: a crew is a company, as of a ship
to vie is to compete or struggle

explanation.surface: Judging a firm with no boss that is about to fight on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking leadership' drops the first letter of the company word; 'about' wraps the result round the struggle word. 'that's' and 'to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To review something is to evaluate or appraise it.

clue.text: Odds in game of rugby slashed at the outset

indicators.note: cut at its start means the rugby game loses its first letter

parts.note: sevens is the seven-a-side form of rugby

explanation.surface: Betting odds on a rugby match that were cut right at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odds' looks like the opposite of the answer, but a bet at evens is still quoted odds.
explanation.definitionFit: Evens is a betting price where the stake is matched, one to one.

clue.text: River bird cradling swallow

indicators.note: cradling means the bird word holds the swallow word inside it

parts.note: a grouse is a game bird
to swallow food is to eat

explanation.surface: A river bird holds a swallow it has caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallow' looks like a second bird; here it is a verb. The Great Ouse is a river in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Ouse is an English river flowing to the Wash, so it is an example.

clue.text: Complete beginner on piccolo with desire for musical ability

parts.note: complete means perfect, as in a perfect stranger

indicators.note: the beginner on piccolo is that word's opening letter

parts.note: an itch is a restless desire

explanation.surface: A total novice on the piccolo who longs to be musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complete beginner' reads as one phrase, but 'Complete' and 'beginner on piccolo' do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfect pitch is the rare talent of naming or singing a note with no reference tone.

clue.text: Is act with iron man generated — using this?

definitions.text: Is act with iron man generated — using this?

indicators.note: generated means these letters are produced in a new order

explanation.surface: A show with a robotic iron man is created by electronic puppetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins IS ACT and IRON MAN, whose letters are rearranged; the whole clue also describes how such a show is made.
explanation.definitionFit: Animatronics is the technique of making lifelike moving figures with motors and electronics.

clue.text: Sure to go after criminal, is one?

definitions.text: Sure to go after criminal, is one?

indicators.note: to go after means the sure word is placed behind the criminal word

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
sure in the sense of steady or secure, stable

explanation.surface: A police officer is always certain to chase down a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go after' reads as pursue, but here it also places one piece behind the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A constable is a police officer, someone whose job is to pursue lawbreakers.

clue.text: Adopting principle at first, one head gives advice

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral

indicators.note: adopting means the one-and-head letters take in the principle letter

parts.note: nut is slang for the head

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of principle

explanation.surface: Someone takes up a principle and offers counsel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' selects P.
explanation.definitionFit: Input is a contribution of ideas or opinion, much like advice.

clue.text: Newspaper slowing down is a problem for the Observer?

parts.note: the i is a British national newspaper
rit is the musical abbreviation of ritardando, slowing down
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper losing pace is troubling for its Sunday rival the Observer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Observer' looks like the British Sunday newspaper; here it is anyone who observes, with eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Iritis is inflammation of the iris, an eye complaint that would trouble someone watching.

clue.text: Team following champion, behind

indicators.note: following means the team word comes after the champion word

parts.note: to champion a cause is to back it
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A sports team trailing the title holder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'champion' looks like a noun; here it is the verb to support.
explanation.definitionFit: Backside and behind are both informal words for the buttocks.

clue.text: One's eyed bait

definitions.meaning: something with an eye, the hole a sewing pin carries thread through
to bait someone is to provoke or goad them

explanation.definitionFit: A sewing needle has an eye, and to needle someone is to tease or provoke them.

clue.text: Howl resulting when wise bird gets this gas?

definitions.text: Howl resulting when wise bird gets this gas?

parts.words: Howl resulting when wise bird gets this gas?
parts.note: the wise bird is an owl; give it the chemical symbol of the gas in front and the word howl appears

explanation.surface: A wise old bird yelps after inhaling some gas.
explanation.walkthrough: The gas's chemical symbol H placed before OWL makes HOWL.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrogen is the gaseous element whose chemical symbol is H.

clue.text: Trunk call doesn't have everyone present

indicators.note: doesn't have means the word call loses the everyone word

parts.note: everyone is all
to present something is to offer it

explanation.surface: A long-distance phone call where not everyone is on the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk call' is an old British term for a long-distance phone call; here 'Trunk' is the definition. CALL without ALL leaves C.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffer is a strongbox or chest, as a trunk is.

clue.text: One million years in pictures

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral
ages means a very long time, years

explanation.surface: A single rare event in a million years captured in photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: Images are pictures or likenesses.

clue.text: Order novel academic award for the Queen Mother

parts.note: the Order of the Bath is a British order of chivalry
She is a novel by H Rider Haggard
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a degree

explanation.surface: An honour, a book and a degree given to the late Queen Mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Queen Mother' suggests Elizabeth, mother of Elizabeth II; here it is the biblical queen.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible Bathsheba became King David's queen and was mother of Solomon.

clue.text: Stuff about English class attributed to performer from Lancashire

indicators.note: about means the stuff word goes round the English letter

parts.note: to stuff oneself is to gorge
a form is a school class
attributed, as a work credited to an author, is marked by

explanation.surface: Filling a lesson on English, credited to a northern entertainer.
explanation.walkthrough: George Formby was a ukulele-playing comic singer and film star from Lancashire, a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: George Formby was a famous entertainer born in Wigan, Lancashire.

clue.text: Still batting, openers from England rarely tested

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is in

indicators.note: the openers of these three words are their first letters

explanation.surface: England's opening batsmen are still at the crease, seldom troubled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'openers' sounds like cricket's opening batsmen; here it means first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert means motionless, as still does.

clue.text: I've had enough stuffing in turkey finally — it's evil!

indicators.note: stuffing means the had-enough phrase fills the other letters
finally takes the last letter of turkey

parts.note: saying I've had enough is saying I quit

explanation.surface: A diner fed up with stuffing in the Christmas turkey condemns it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuffing' looks like the turkey's filling but places I QUIT inside IN plus Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Iniquity is wickedness or sin, evil conduct.

clue.text: We held tight entering Northern Ireland capital

indicators.note: entering means the rearranged letters go inside the abbreviation
tight means drunk, so the letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: We clung on hard as we came into Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' looks like holding firmly but means drunk: EWDELH, an anagram of WE HELD, enters NI.
explanation.definitionFit: New Delhi is the capital city of India.

clue.text: Sad about recent changes over new commemoration of time past

indicators.note: about means the sad word goes round the other letters

parts.note: teary means tearful, sad

indicators.note: in a down entry over means the rearranged letters sit above the new letter
changes means recent is rearranged

explanation.surface: Mourning recent changes rather than celebrating history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' shuffles the clue word recent; 'over', in a down entry, sets those letters above N; 'about' wraps the sad word around everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A tercentenary is a three-hundredth anniversary, marking events of long ago.

clue.text: One dining out as an art thief?

parts.note: a pic is a picture, a piece of art
a nicker is someone who nicks, British slang for steals

explanation.surface: A stylish eater out who doubles as a painting thief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dining out' is eating in the open air, not at a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A picnicker eats a meal outdoors, literally dining out.

clue.text: Order contains restrictive measure

indicators.note: to order the letters is to arrange them afresh, so contains is reshuffled

explanation.surface: An instruction that includes a limiting rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like the definition; it is the signal to rearrange 'contains'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanction is a penalty such as a trade embargo imposed to restrict a country.

clue.text: VIP report?

definitions.meaning: a very important person, a bigwig
a report is a loud bang, a large sound

explanation.definitionFit: A big noise is slang for an important person, and literally a loud report.

clue.text: Jump three months, approximately?

definitions.meaning: a season of roughly a quarter of the year

explanation.definitionFit: To spring is to jump, and spring is a season of about three months.

clue.text: Edited news report's outside broadcast

indicators.note: edited means these letters are reworked into a new order
the outside of report is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A revised news report was transmitted from an outside broadcast unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside broadcast' reads as one TV phrase; 'outside' gives R and T of report, joining NEWS for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcast in its old sense of sown widely means scattered, as strewn does.

clue.text: Cabaret singer ends poorly in quaver

indicators.note: the ends here are the last letters of cabaret and singer

parts.note: poorly means unwell, ill

explanation.surface: A nightclub vocalist finishes weakly, with a shaky voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quaver' suggests the musical note; here it is a warbling sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A trill is a rapid wavering between two notes, a quaver in the voice.
